q: The standard warranty clause in railway supply contracts generally covers how long from the date of commissioning?
The alternative leg of the warranty period is generally how many months from the date of supply?
Which of the following is normally covered under the warranty clause of a railway supply contract?
A performance guarantee under a railway contract primarily assures the purchaser about what?
Which agency is generally nominated as the inspection agency for railway stores contracts?
Inspection of stores before despatch at the supplier's works is called what?
When stores are rejected during inspection, the document issued to the supplier is generally called what?
Rejected stores lying at the consignee's depot must normally be removed by the supplier within what period?
If rejected stores are not removed within the stipulated period, the railway may levy what?
Replacement of rejected stores is normally required to be made by the supplier at whose cost?
The standard rate of liquidated damages for delayed supply in IRS conditions of contract is generally what?
The maximum ceiling for liquidated damages under standard IRS conditions is generally what?

A warranty claim must normally be raised on the contractor within what period?
After replacement of a defective component under warranty, the warranty period for the replaced part is generally what?

options.C: A fresh period as per contract

q: Latent defects discovered after acceptance of stores are generally dealt with under which clause?
Rectification of defects during the warranty period is normally carried out by the contractor at what cost?
Acceptance of stores by the consignee after inspection does not extinguish the contractor's what?

options.D: Warranty liability continues for latent defects

q: Replacement stores offered by the supplier against rejection are generally what?
If the replacement of rejected stores is delayed beyond the stipulated period, the railway may levy what?
After rejection at inspection, the rejected stores are generally required to be what?

options.D: Marked or segregated to prevent re-offer

q: The decision of the nominated inspection agency regarding acceptance or rejection is generally considered what?
On what primary ground can stores be rejected during inspection?
Facilities for inspection and testing at the supplier's works are normally provided to the inspecting officer at what cost?
A warranty claim is normally raised in writing on whom?
An inspection certificate issued after inspection is evidence of what?
An inspection call for pre-despatch inspection must normally be given with what?
Rejected stores not removed by the supplier within the stipulated period may be what?

options.C: Disposed of by auction or tender

q: The cost of removing rejected stores from the consignee's premises is normally borne by whom?
For plant and machinery, the warranty period generally commences from what date?
Which of the following is normally NOT covered under the warranty clause?

options.D: Misuse or improper handling by the user

q: A warranty bank guarantee furnished by the contractor is intended to secure what?
Stores found defective on receipt at the consignee depot may be what?
Disputes relating to warranty claims and rejection are generally settled how?

options.D: Settled as per contract and arbitration clause

q: Failure of the contractor to honour warranty obligations may lead to what action against the security deposit?
The warranty period for spare parts supplied under a contract is generally what?
Where the contract includes erection and commissioning, these are normally the responsibility of whom?
Rejected stores lying at the depot pending removal by the supplier are normally what?

options.C: Kept separate, not taken on stock

q: Charges for tests carried out during inspection are generally which of the following?

options.D: Borne by the supplier as per contract

q: When stores received at the depot are short or damaged, the consignee normally issues what?
Latent defects discovered in service must be notified to the contractor within what time?
Granting an extension of time for replacement supply to the contractor generally has what effect?

options.D: It does not waive LD unless expressly stated

q: Inspection during the course of manufacture is generally conducted for what purpose?
Stores failing the inspection on the first offer are subject to what?
Stores rectified and re-offered after rejection are generally what?
The warranty period after rectification or replacement is generally what?
Consumable and perishable stores generally carry what kind of warranty?
Warranty claims are normally processed and pursued by whom?
A replacement guarantee under a warranty clause generally assures what?
Persistent failure to honour warranty obligations may lead to what action?

options.B: Cancellation of contract at contractor's risk
